fields.value: Level up the evaluation API: seats drawn from a pool, training that reads the population, a rating over every checkpoint

Jack Heart, 2026-11-13: "Okay let's just file all these as one task, which is just 'Level Up Evaluation API.'" Not urgent; it follows EXP-56.

## Why

Evaluation is where Etude differs from a tracker. Jack Heart, 2026-11-13: "one of the biggest places we're differentiating is the focus on evals... this idea of multi-agent evals is about being able to generate evals where you're comparing different checkpoints with each other in certain environments", and the environment includes "what are the other policies that are in the situation... there are more different policies that are being trained and it's more evolutionary".

Main at v0.3.1 already has Seating, relative seats (Earlier, Fraction, At, Final, Aligned), Crosstable, and `observe(source, experiment)`. Three things are missing.

## The three gaps

1. A seat that draws from a pool. Every seat today resolves to exactly one player. Nothing says "an opponent, or teammates, drawn from this set of checkpoints", with the draw recorded. This is the population case ("how does this checkpoint do against the field") and the measure of a player's value averaged over random teammates. It is the one real gap in the evaluation model.
2. Training has no documented way to read the population. `observe(source, experiment)` returns every run's checkpoints, so a loop could call it today, but there is no guidance for doing so from inside training and no record of which opponents a run trained against. Manabot's frozen-opponent training was retired in the MTG-329 cutover, so nothing currently exercises this.
3. No rating across the whole population. Scores are curves per seating, and round robins give standings for hand-picked entrants. There is no single table over every checkpoint of an experiment.

## Outcome

A design covering the three together, since they share one idea (a set of checkpoints as a first-class thing a seat, a training loop and a report can each name), then delivery. Open for the design: how a pool is named and frozen so a draw replays; whether lineage (who a run trained against) is a row table or a run field; which rating, and how it stays comparable as the population grows; whether game setup stays an opaque `conditions` value.

## Constraints

Paired deals, replay verification and seeds as the unit of evidence keep working. Existing Seating and report names stay; this adds to them.

## Context

`docs/evaluation.md`, `src/etude/report.py`. Positioning notes: `scratch/positioning.md` in the Manabot worktree `manabot.aa55a0-move-run-execution` (MTG-329).
